## Finding

**P2 / PERF-239-01: move the rewritten prompt instead of deep-copying it.** `crates/cache-proxy/src/proxy.rs:579-584` calls `rewritten.body.clone()` through `as_ref()`. That field is `Option<Vec<u8>>`, so every changed Messages body incurs another full-payload allocation and memcpy after JSON serialization. The original serialized vector remains in `rewritten`, which is used again for log metadata at lines 683-685, across the upstream `.send().await`. This adds O(body bytes) work and retained payload storage per concurrent rewritten request on the shared sidecar. It affects normal cache-TTL/model rewrites, not just an error path; at ten approximately 64 MiB rewritten requests the duplicate alone is approximately 640 MiB. That is a size illustration, not a measured RSS result.

**Fix:** destructure `Rewritten`, or take its body out, and move that vector into `Bytes::from`, retaining only the initiator/model/count metadata. Keep the existing `Bytes::clone()` at line 633 for the single retry: that clone shares the payload. This does not require introducing a streaming JSON rewriter. The existing buffering/DOM parse has its own O(body bytes) cost; this finding is specifically the redundant second serialized payload.

No process-rate blocker found.

## Cost inventory

| Surface | Rate and scaling |
|---|---|
| Forward/retry loop | One upstream attempt per request, at most one retry after a 401 with a newer token. No launch on the ordinary request path. Work scales with request bytes and active requests, not idle seats. Response chunks stream through; the usage logger collects only an initial prefix before releasing it. |
| Token launch | Absolute-path `gh`; one fetch when a configured sidecar starts, on account change, or on reload after missing/failed token retrieval. The refresh mutex and token generation share one refresh across the same-generation 401 burst. A failed refresh latches until reload. Recorded as `gh.cache_proxy_token`. No periodic token refresh. |
| Readiness | Lazy, serialized checks: one user GET and one models GET per 600 s while healthy and asked; failure-cache lifetime 60 s, with up to two GETs per attempt. Startup/reload and invalidation after successful refresh or a 402 can cause additional checks. No independent readiness timer and no launch; one account, not per seat. |
| Human-account check | One absolute `/usr/bin/dscl` per manual CLI `status`; recorded as `dscl.cache_proxy_accounts`. HTTP status itself does not launch dscl. |
| Listener/connections | Event-driven accept loop and one Tokio task per accepted connection, not an OS process. Header-read timeout 60 s; unexpected accept errors back off 1 s; shutdown drains for up to 15 s. No per-seat polling. |
| Operation deadlines | In-process timers only: upstream connect 10 s, each readiness GET 15 s, gh completion 15 s; manual CLI status 5 s and reload 60 s. None is a periodic launch. |
| LaunchAgent | One machine-wide sidecar, RunAtLoad/KeepAlive, restart throttle 10 s. `/bin/sh` execs the absolute installed binary. Startup/restart cost is constant with seats; installer commands are manual, not a tick path. |

Both production child-launch sites call `pij_core::spawns::record`; `spawn_sites.rs` now includes `cache-proxy`. Daemon spawn counters are process-local and do not by themselves establish the separate sidecar's launch count.

## Evidence

`just pr-freeze 239`: **FINAL**, matching full head, clean detached worktree, CLEAN merge state and all five checks passing. `gh run view 44225036106 --log`: exact-head CI succeeded. `cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed; `cargo nextest run --locked --workspace --profile ci` passed, 2,465 tests with six skipped. Successful rust-test job 134536017451 uploaded artifact **14391968226**; downloaded by ID and inspected its JUnit: **26 sidecar tests and all six spawn_sites tests passed**, including single-flight refresh, failed-refresh latch and launch recording.

Author receipts in `docs/plans/228-cache-proxy-sidecar/assets/evidence/live-rows.md`: row 17 records ten clients, requests 0 -> 10 and gh launches 1 -> 1; row 9 records three concurrent stale-token clients sharing one refresh, total gh launches 2; row 11 records nine 401s with only startup plus one failed refresh. The packet also records daemon spawns 475 -> 475 over 20 s and a 96.1 launches/s machine window. These are author-recorded feature receipts, not newly repeated experiments.

Independent read-only production baseline, 2026-11-18 02:45:51-02:46:11 UTC: daemon PID 46800 and start identity unchanged; `pij-rs --json ping` spawns **548 -> 548** across 20.225 s, every by-op delta zero. `just spawn-rate --seconds 20 --json`: **113.3 launches/s** machine-wide, daemon-child sampled lower bound empty. `/bin/ps` cumulative daemon CPU **5:45.12 -> 5:49.36** (4.24 CPU s, approximately 21% of one core); RSS **151008 -> 153568 KiB** (147.47 -> 149.97 MiB). The sampler adds load. This is a current baseline, not a feature-on CPU/RSS measurement; 96.1 and 113.3 are not a controlled before/after pair.

No local build, test compilation, full `harness checks`, production restart, deployment, or sidecar startup was performed. Build/test proof is the exact-head CI as requested. This verdict covers resource cost, not correctness, security, or model-spend acceptance.

## Harness feedback

Difficulty: launch-only short-prompt receipts do not expose per-request prompt-buffer amplification. Magic wand: extend the existing fake-upstream cost scenario with large prompts and concurrent clients, recording peak RSS and latency alongside launch counters. This is the highest-value follow-up proof improvement; a new benchmark framework or streaming-parser redesign is not required for PERF-239-01.
